items.excerpt: Published 2026.11.12. 13:21:01 ... ■ Big-step debate: Christopher Waller, a governor of the U.S. Federal Reserve, said the Fed should consider raising its benchmark rate by 0.50 percentage points at its December meeting if October core consumer price index growth came in at or above roughly 0.3%. The CPI released shortly after his speech met that condition exactly. Energy price gains have slowed, but price pressure has spread to transportation services, food and housing costs. A string of hawkish comments from Fed officials sent New York stocks broadly lower, and the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.021% during the session. ... Waller Floats a December Half-Point Hike, but AI Sentiment and Oil Cloud the Outlook - Key points: Fed Governor Waller said the central bank should consider a half-point hike in December if October core CPI came in near 0.3%, and the reading released just after his remarks met that bar, strengthening the case inside the Fed for a larger move. Waller said raising rates by only 0.25 percentage points could jeopardize the Fed's credibility, and Dallas Federal Reserve Bank President Lorie Logan also argued for at least two quarter-point increases. The two-year Treasury yield jumped 0.18 percentage points in a single day to 4.74%. Even so, CME FedWatch pricing put the probability of a December hike at 100% but the odds of a 0.50-percentage-point move at just 13.2%, leaving the prevailing view that the Fed will moderate its pace given the surge in corporate bond yields and the deterioration in AI investment sentiment.

items.title: U.S. attorney demands Sen. Richard Blumenthal preserve documents from his inquiry into White House ballroom
items.excerpt: Nov. 11, 2026, 9:11 PM EST By Raquel Coronell Uribe, Ryan J. Reilly and Frank Thorp V A Justice Department official called on Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., on Wednesday to preserve documents related to what he claims is harassment of citizens during Blumenthal’s investigation into White House ballroom donors, threatening “significant legal consequences” if he does not comply. The U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, Aaron Reitz, alleged in a letter to Blumenthal that his investigation equated to threatening “citizens for associating themselves with the President and other public officials.” The White House warned congressional Democrats on Wednesday that efforts to investigate the administration could be a crime. In a post on X with a copy of the letter attached, Reitz equated Blumenthal’s investigation examining anonymous donors for the roughly $400 million project on White House grounds with wielding Congress as a “weapon” against Americans. “I’m taking the first step to stop this abuse of power,” Reitz said. Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter, the second-highest-ranking official at the Justice Department, responded to Reitz’s post, saying, “The First Amendment expressly prohibits Congress from infringing the speech and association rights of Americans.” “DOJ will defend against threats to those rights, period,” McCotter wrote. Blumenthal said in a statement responding to the letter that he “will not be intimidated,” vowing to “vigorously pursue investigations into this Administration’s persistent misuse of taxpayer dollars and any corporate entity that has enabled their boundless corruption.” “The Trump Administration is so afraid of transparency and oversight that they are weaponizing the Department of Justice to baselessly target Congress in direct violation of the Constitution,” Blumenthal wrote. Blumenthal is the top Democrat on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. The subcommittee is tasked with studying the economics and efficiency of government operations. Blumenthal sent letters last month to a list of people whom a Washington Post report identified as having donated private funds to the ballroom’s construction. A news release said he was “leading an inquiry into waste, fraud, and abuse associated with the White House ballroom and other projects throughout the nation’s capital.” President Donald Trump had vowed to release the names of the private donors, but he has made only a partial list public. A few donors have acknowledged their donations, including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who is under investigation by the company and the FBI for an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Trump defended Huang in remarks to reporters this week. Reitz’s letter cited the federal conspiracy against rights statute, as well as the federal deprivation of rights under color of law statute. Such an overt investigative measure against a sitting member of Congress would typically have undergone an extensive review process within the Justice Department’s Public Integrity Office, but that office has been shrunk and sidelined in the second Trump term. A Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement that “the Department routinely requests that records be preserved when public officials take such extreme actions,” alleging that Blumenthal’s letters were an attempt to “suppress their First Amendment activities, including their philanthropic practices.” ... Blumenthal on Wednesday night responded to Reitz’s letter with a record preservation request of his own, calling his efforts to investigate the ballroom donations “appropriate” and part of his “constitutional duties.” “Since you appear to have evidence of the Trump Administration’s efforts to protect corporate donors and Administration officials from legitimate oversight, I accordingly direct you to preserve all records and correspondence, including all communications with the White House or senior officials at the Department of Justice, related to the decision to draft and post your letter,” Blumenthal wrote.

items.title: White House faces unusual obstacle on confirming Trump judges: other Republicans | WBAL Baltimore News
items.excerpt: - November 11, 2026 WASHINGTON (AP) — Several Republican senators are complicating a White House plan to leave an enduring imprint on the judiciary long after President Donald Trump leaves office by throwing up obstacles for a handful of his judicial nominees in the final weeks of their Senate majority. In Texas, outgoing Sen. John Cornyn has expressed reservations about a top Justice Department official who has been nominated for a federal judgeship in the Dallas area. The two Arkansas senators, both Republicans, opposed a Trump nominee to a powerful appeals court seat, forcing the White House to withdraw Trump’s pick this week. And in Oklahoma, an appointed GOP senator has thrown up sudden objections to a district court nominee after earlier giving him the green light. Central to this effort are Cornyn and retiring North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis, both of whom serve on the Judiciary Committee and are using their leverage to effectively block nominations on behalf of Republicans who aren’t on the panel. Though it comes after the midterm losses that weakened Trump’s political standing, this under-the-radar judiciary fight is more about Republicans asserting their powers over the administration’s judge selections, which has long been a cherished prerogative for senators , particularly for their home states. Asked about his opposition to the Arkansas and Oklahoma nominees, Tillis said he wants senators and their views on the prospective judges to be heard by the administration. His message to the White House, Tillis said, was: “Don’t treat us like a manufacturing facility. Treat us like the U.S. Senate.” “I’m not making a judgment about the merit of the nominee. I’m calling a foul on a process,” Tillis said in an interview with the Associated Press. “And the sooner the White House gets that, the more productive this next two years will be. If they don’t, they do so at their own peril.” Trump had nominated Lee Rudofsky of Arkansas to the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals. But the White House abruptly pulled that nomination on Tuesday, after Cornyn and Tillis had privately conveyed to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, that they would vote against Rudofsky in committee, according to two people with knowledge of the discussions who spoke on condition of anonymity to confirm private deliberations. Grassley also was forced to postpone a key committee vote on Tuesday for Oklahoma judicial nominee Zachary West because of opposition from Tillis on behalf of Sen. items.title: K-pop News Today (Nov 12, 2026): Coachella 2027, BTS, IVE, RESCENE
items.excerpt: ## JISOO, NCT and BABYMONSTER Are Heading to Coachella 2027 BLACKPINK’s JISOO, NCT and BABYMONSTER are on the lineup for Coachella 2027, which the festival announced on Nov. 10 (local time), Yonhap and Kyunghyang Shinmun reported on Nov. 11. JISOO plays on April 9 and 16, NCT on April 10 and 17, and BABYMONSTER on April 11 and 18 in Indio, California. Pansori-pop band Leenalchi and Berlin-based Korean DJ Peggy Gou are also on the bill, with Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA as headliners and Madonna on the lineup too. JISOO has played Coachella with BLACKPINK in 2019 and 2023, when the group became the first K-pop act to headline, and this time she returns as a soloist. NCT are listed simply as “NCT,” with no unit named, and it will be their first Coachella. For BABYMONSTER, it is the dream stage they have talked about since their early days, coming about three years after their official debut in April 2024, and Edaily noted they are the first fifth-generation K-pop group to make the lineup. ... ## BTS’s “SWIM” Is the Only K-pop Group Song on Apple Music’s “Best Songs of 2026” “SWIM,” the title track of BTS’s fifth full album “ARIRANG,” made Apple Music’s “Best Songs of 2026,” a list of 100 songs announced on Nov. 7 (local time), BIGHIT MUSIC said on Nov. 11, as Yonhap and Newsis reported. BTS are the only K-pop group on the list, and “SWIM” also appears on Apple Music’s A-List Pop, Viral Hits and KPOPWRLD year-end playlists. “BTS’s ‘ARIRANG’ comeback was a moment K-pop had long been waiting for,” Apple Music wrote, adding that the group “redefined the flow of K-pop in 2026.” JENNIE’s feature on Tame Impala’s “Dracula” and pianist Lim Yunchan’s live Carnegie Hall recording of Bach’s “Goldberg Variations” made the list too. The album is still going strong in the US: “ARIRANG” sits at No. 62 on the Billboard 200 dated Nov. 14, its 33rd straight week on the chart, and “SWIM” climbed five spots to No. 28 on the Global 200. The “SWIM” MV had 174,235,286 views when we checked. ARMY, the “ARIRANG” tour heads to Southeast Asia next, starting in Kaohsiung on Nov. 19. ... ## IVE Enter the Billboard 200 for the First Time and Top the Emerging Artists Chart IVE’s mini album “Looks Can Kill” entered the Billboard 200 at No. 126 on the chart dated Nov. 14, the group’s first time on Billboard’s main album chart, Top Star News and OSEN reported on Nov. 11. IVE also reached No. 1 on the Emerging Artists chart and re-entered the Artist 100 at No. 66. The album placed No. 2 on World Albums, No. 6 on Top Album Sales and No. 19 on Independent Albums, all higher than their last album “REVIVE+,” and the title track spent a second week on the Global Excl. U.S. chart. It comes about four years and 11 months after their debut in December 2021, and after a world tour that wrapped in August and grew their North American run from six cities to eight, all in arenas. At home, “Looks Can Kill” topped Circle Chart’s weekly album and retail album charts, and IVE held No. 1 on Hanteo’s world chart for a third straight week. ... ## RESCENE Win “Show Champion” and Announce Their First Solo Concert RESCENE won first place on MBC M’s “Show Champion” on Nov. 11 with “With,” their second music show trophy in two days after SBS LIFE’s “THE SHOW” on Nov. 10, Top Star News reported. “I think we could win this because Remine are always right beside us, loving us the most,” WONI said on stage. The same day, the group announced “2027 RESCENE CONCERT IN SEOUL,” their first solo concert, set for Feb. 19 to 21, 2027, at Olympic Hall in Seoul’s Olympic Park, MK Sports reported. “Holding our first solo concert, which we’ve wished for since debut, feels like a dream,” the members said, and tickets open in December through the Coupang Play app. Three years in, RESCENE are finally getting the stage of their own that fans have been asking for. ... ## LISA’s Documentary “Always Lalisa” and New Song “Leave With Me” Arrive on Nov. 18 LISA’s documentary “Always Lalisa,” which follows her year of solo work, will stream exclusively on YouTube Premium from Nov. 18, YouTube announced on its official blog on Nov. 10 (local time), Sports Kyunghyang reported on Nov. 11. “Leave With Me,” the song made for the film and first heard over its end credits in theaters, gets its official release the same day.
